'''Andre Emmett''' (August 27, 1982 – September 23, 2019) was an American professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech Red Raiders]], and was named a consensus [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] as a senior in 2004. He had brief stints in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] and the [[New Jersey Nets]] after being selected in the second round of the [[2004 NBA draft]]. Emmett was shot to death on September 23, 2019, in Dallas.

==College career==
Emmett played [[college basketball]] for 4 years for [[Bob Knight]] at [[Texas Tech University]]. He is currently the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Red Raiders]]' all-time leading scorer and the 3rd all-time leading scorer in the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] behind Buddy Hield and LaceDarius Dunn with 2,256 points. During his freshman year and playing for Coach James Dickey, Emmett earned his way into the starting lineup averaging 7.7 points and 3.6 rebounds per game. When [[Bob Knight]] arrived at Texas Tech in 2001, Emmett saw his scoring average improve to 18.7 which was good enough for 3rd in the conference behind Drew Gooden and Kareem Rush and 1st team All-Big 12 honors. His junior and senior year, Emmett proved to be one of the best scorers in college basketball averaging 21.8 and 20.6 points per game, respectively. He also earned Unanimous 1st team All-Big 12 honors his junior and senior year and consensus [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors his senior year. Emmett capped off his college career by winning the 2004 NCAA Slam Dunk Contest.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.texastech.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/emmett_andre01.html|title=Andre Emmett Profile|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202123943/http://www.texastech.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/emmett_andre01.html|archive-date=2014-02-02}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===2004–05 season===
Emmett was selected by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] with the 35th overall pick in the [[2004 NBA draft]]. He was later traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in a draft night trade. He joined the Grizzlies for 2004 NBA Summer League. On July 7, 2004, he signed his first professional contract with the Grizzlies. In the 2004–05 season, he played a total of 8 games for the Grizzlies.

===2005–06 season===
Emmett re-joined the Grizzlies for the 2005 NBA Summer League. On August 3, 2005, Emmett was traded to the Miami Heat in a five-team trade involving the Memphis Grizzlies, Miami Heat, Boston Celtics, Utah Jazz, and New Orleans Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_acquire_walkerwilliamsposey_050803.html|title=HEAT Acquire Antoine Walker, Jason Williams & James Posey|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2019-09-24|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190924084914/https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heatacquirewalkerwilliamsposey050803html|archive-date=2019-09-24}}</ref> On October 31, 2005, he was waived by the Heat. In November 2005, he was acquired by the Austin Toros of the [[NBA D-League]].

===2006–07 season===
In July 2006, Emmett joined the Dallas Mavericks for the [[NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]] and the Seattle SuperSonics for the [[Rocky Mountain Revue]]. Later that year, he signed with a Lithuanian club [[BC Lietuvos rytas]] for the 2006–07 season. In December 2006, he left Lietuvos rytas. On January 19, 2007, he was acquired by the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_06-07.html |title=2006-07 Transactions |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-01-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150618011602/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_06-07.html |archive-date=2015-06-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===2007–08 season===
Emmett joined the Houston Rockets for the 2007 NBA Summer League. In December 2007, he signed with the [[Liège Basket]] of Belgium for the rest of the 2007–08 season, subsequently finishing the best scorer (23.9 ppg) of the Belgian championship.

===2008–09 season===
Emmett joined the Indiana Pacers for the 2008 NBA Summer League. On September 29, 2008, he signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. However, he was waived by the 76ers on October 6. Later that month, he joined [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Orthez]] of France for the 2008–09 season. In January 2009, he left Pau-Orthez after playing in only 5 games. He later joined [[Marinos de Anzoátegui]] for the 2009 LPB season.

===2009–10 season===
In November 2009, he signed with the [[Shandong Lions]] of [[Chinese Basketball Association|China]] for the 2009–10 season. In March 2010, he scored a (then) CBA-record 71 points in a game against the [[Jiangsu Dragons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.163.com/10/0308/06/6180OL01000146BB.html|title=艾米特71分创CBA纪录]|language=zh|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170707150047/http://news.163.com/10/0308/06/6180OL01000146BB.html|archive-date=2017-07-07|access-date=2010-03-08}}</ref> Following the CBA season, he joined [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] for the rest of the 2010 BSN season.

===2010–11 season===
In December 2010, he signed with [[Fujian Xunxing]] of China for the rest of the 2010–11 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/19380/fujian-adds-scoring-machine-andre-emmett.html|title=Fujian adds scoring machine Andre Emmett|website=sportando.net|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201212926/http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/19380/fujian-adds-scoring-machine-andre-emmett.html|archive-date=2014-02-01|access-date=2014-01-21}}</ref> On March 25, 2011, he was acquired by the [[Reno Bighorns]].

===2011–12 season===
On December 15, 2011, he was re-acquired by the Bighorns. On February 14, 2012, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Jersey Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/02/14/nets-emmett.ap/ |title=Injury-plagued Nets sign F Andre Emmett to 10-day contract |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2012-02-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203024454/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/02/14/nets-emmett.ap/ |archive-date=2014-02-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On February 24, 2012, he returned to the Bighorns. In April 2012, he signed with [[Sporting Al Riyadi Beirut]] of Lebanon for the 2012 [[Lebanese Basketball League|FLB League]] playoffs.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/38072/al-riyadi-andre-emmett-replaces-dewarick-spencer.html|title=Al-Riyadi, Andre Emmett replaces Dewarick Spencer|website=sportando.net|url-status=dead|access-date=2014-01-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201212921/http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/38072/al-riyadi-andre-emmett-replaces-dewarick-spencer.html|archive-date=2014-02-01}}</ref>

===2012–13 season===
Emmett joined the NBA D-League Select Team for the 2012 NBA Summer League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/summerleague/bio/andre_emmett.html|title=NBA Development League: 2012 Select Team Bio: Andre Emmett|website=nba.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160712122349/http://www.nba.com/dleague/summerleague/bio/andre_emmett.html|archive-date=2016-07-12|access-date=2014-01-21}}</ref> On October 1, 2012, he signed with the Chicago Bulls. However, he was waived by the Bulls on October 15.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-guard-andre-emmett.html|title=Bulls waive guard Andre Emmett|website=nba.com|access-date=2019-09-24|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203024504/http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-guard-andre-emmett.html|archive-date=2014-02-03}}</ref>

In December 2012, Emmett signed with [[Amchit Club]] of Lebanon for the rest of the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/47643/andre-emmett-signs-in-lebanon-with-amchit.html|title=Andre Emmett signs in Lebanon with Amchit|website=sportando.net|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201212923/http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/47643/andre-emmett-signs-in-lebanon-with-amchit.html|archive-date=2014-02-01|access-date=2014-01-21}}</ref> Following the FLB League season, he joined [[Cocodrilos de Caracas]] for the 2013 LPB season, but left after 5 games.

===2013–14 season===
In January 2014, Emmett joined Cocodrilos de Caracas for the [[2014 FIBA Americas League]]. In April 2014, he joined [[Halcones Rojos Veracruz]] of Mexico before re-joining Cocodrilos de Caracas for the 2014 LPB season. On July 13, 2014, he signed with [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] where he played one game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/127102/piratas-de-quebradillas-sign-andre-emmett.html|title=Piratas de Quebradillas sign Andre Emmett|website=sportando.net|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304081606/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/127102/piratas-de-quebradillas-sign-andre-emmett.html|archive-date=2016-03-04|access-date=2014-07-14}}</ref>

===2014–15 season===
On November 1, 2014, Emmett was selected by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] in the second round of the 2014 NBA D-League draft.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/fortwayne/mad_ants_finalize_201415_trai_2014_11_02.html |title=Mad Ants Finalize 2014-15 Training Camp Roster |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-11-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104220255/http://www.nba.com/dleague/fortwayne/mad_ants_finalize_201415_trai_2014_11_02.html |archive-date=2014-11-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On February 4, 2015, he was named to the Futures All-Star team for the 2015 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star Game]], the second time in his career.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters-2015/|title=Thirteen NBA Veterans Headline Rosters for NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented by Kumho Tire|date=February 15, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=February 15, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150205023335/http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters-2015/|archive-date=February 5, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> He went on to record 28 points, 4 rebounds and 4 steals, and was subsequently named the All-Star Game MVP.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wane.com/2015/02/15/emmett-nets-28-named-nbadl-all-star-game-mvp/|title=Emmett Nets 28, Named NBADL All-Star Game MVP|website=wane.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304053704/http://wane.com/2015/02/15/emmett-nets-28-named-nbadl-all-star-game-mvp/|archive-date=2016-03-04|access-date=2015-02-17}}</ref>

On March 5, 2015, Andre Emmett left the Mad Ants and signed with the [[Meralco Bolts]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] for the [[2015 PBA Governors' Cup|2015 Governor's Cup]] campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.texastech.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031815aaa.html|title=Former Red Raiders Shining Abroad|website=texastech.com|access-date=2019-09-24|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150423115017/http://www.texastech.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031815aaa.html|archive-date=2015-04-23}}</ref>

===2015–16 season===
On July 22, 2015, Emmett was selected by the KCC EGIS([[전주 KCC 이지스]]) with the 5th overall pick in the [[2015 KBL foreigner draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sports.news.naver.com/basketball/news/read.nhn?oid=065&aid=0000110985|title="1순위였어도 에밋" KCC에 주어진 과제|website=sports.news.naver.com}}</ref>

==Death==
Emmett died on September 23, 2019, after being [[Gunshot wound|shot]] during an armed robbery in [[Dallas|Dallas, Texas]]. He was taken to a hospital where he was later pronounced dead. He was 37 years old.<ref>{{cite news|title=Former NBA Player Andre Emmett Found Dead In Dallas|date=September 23, 2019|website=CBSDFW.com|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/dfw/news/former-nba-player-andre-emmett-found-dead-in-dallas/|access-date=September 23, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Dallas hoops star Andre Emmett found dead in Old East Dallas|date=September 23, 2019|website=dallasnews.com|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/news/crime/2019/09/23/reports-dallas-hoops-star-andre-emmett-found-dead-in-old-east-dallas/|author= Cassandra Jaramillo|access-date=September 23, 2019}}</ref>
